title: Walter Page versus Blanton, and Phil Moore the atheist
summary: Page's two-note lines against Blanton's melodic walking; church singing and Phil Moore's atheism.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: I would say that (inaudible) influence on me, too, because I saw his name on so many films. I would listen to his music and buy some of his backgrounds that he wrote tried to play like (inaudible) Walter Page although I accepted him, because he was sliding on that one and I (inaudible) string. I never respected him too much, when I was younger. But I did understand that he did know what he was doing and he could swing, as I grew older. He did contribute to bass playing. (inaudible) Most bass players were playing like Walter Page, (singing), two notes. Jimmy Blanton used to come in playing, (singing). He would run the scale now and then, but (inaudible) you'd call it a melodic line, melodic walking line. Let me see who influenced me. I guess you could say Church, to an extent. Not that I was proud of it or anything. I remember when I was studying with Phil Moore one time, told me that he was -- it was a hot day in California and so the window was open, and you'd hear these church people out there singing real loud, Yonder Jesus Christ. And Phil scared me because he was an atheist. He said, "Why don't these bastards wake up? When they're dead, they're dead, dead and we're living, they're right where they belong. That's why (inaudible) because their mentality is so limited, OR somewhere else to go because they think that there's a heaven," I didn't want to get

in a fight with him because I thought there was a heaven also. Maybe that's why I'm so dumb, because I figure there's got to be something better than this. Where the game is not for real or for fair, that somewhere else there must be a game going on when you're doing something, with human beings that's for real for for fair, (inaudible) you're accepted and get a chance to do it. Why do you have to wait 25 years to record a composition? I'm still in the red on my record dates. I haven't made no money on the records yet.
